title: The adjoint section of the normalized universal module
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field, let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over $k$ with a $k$-rational point $\sigma$, let $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$, and let $D_{\mathrm{univ}}\subset H\times_kX$ be the universal effective Cartier divisor [lem-pc-universal-divisor]. Put $\mathcal L_H:=\mathcal O(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\otimes\operatorname{pr}_H^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal O(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}$. Let $W\subseteq H$ be the maximal open on which $\mathcal L_H|_{W\times_kX}$ belongs to the Picard open subfunctor $F(W)$ [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor], and write $f_W:W\times_kX\to W$ and $\mathcal N_W:=f_{W,*}(\mathcal L_H|_{W\times_kX})$. Then $\mathcal N_W$ is invertible and the section corresponding under tensor--Hom adjunction to the counit $f_W^*\mathcal N_W\to\mathcal L_H|_{W\times_kX}$ has zero scheme $D_{\mathrm{univ}}|_{W\times_kX}$.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor] the inclusion $F\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable by open immersions; applied to $\mathcal L_H\in\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(H)$ this gives the maximal open $W\subseteq H$ with $\mathcal L_W:=\mathcal L_H|_{W\times X}\in F(W)$. By the definition of $F$ there is an invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module $\mathcal N$ with $Rf_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N[0]$; taking $H^0$, $\mathcal N_W=f_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N$ is invertible and $Rf_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N_W[0]$. Let $\varphi:f_W^*\mathcal N_W\to\mathcal L_W$ be the counit and $s_{\mathrm{adj}}$ the corresponding section of $\mathcal L_W\otimes f_W^*\mathcal N_W^{-1}$; its zero scheme is $Z(\varphi)$ [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso]. The hypotheses of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd] ($T=W$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_W\in F(W)$, $\mathcal N=\mathcal N_W$ invertible with $Rf_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N_W[0]$) hold, so $Z(\varphi)$ is a closed subscheme of $W\times X$ finite locally free of degree $g$ over $W$, i.e. a point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$.

proof.text: Write $D_W:=D_{\mathrm{univ}}|_{W\times X}$ and $\mathcal M:=\sigma_W^*\mathcal O(D_W)^{-1}$, so $\mathcal L_W=\mathcal O(D_W)\otimes f_W^*\mathcal M$ by definition. By [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme] the canonical section $1_D$ of $\mathcal O(D_W)$ has $Z(1_D)=D_W$; hence $s_1:=1_D\otimes\mathrm{id}:f_W^*\mathcal M\to\mathcal L_W$ has $Z(s_1)=D_W$ (locally $s_1$ is multiplication by the same local equation, $f_W^*\mathcal M$ being invertible). By adjunction $s_1=\varphi\circ f_W^*t$ for $t:\mathcal M\to f_{W,*}\mathcal L_W$ adjoint to $s_1$; locally $s_1$ is multiplication by $b\,c$ where $\varphi$ is multiplication by $b$, so $\mathcal I_{Z(s_1)}\subseteq\mathcal I_{Z(\varphi)}$, i.e. $Z(\varphi)\subseteq D_W$. Since $D_{\mathrm{univ}}$ is the universal point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}$ [lem-pc-universal-divisor], $D_W$ is also a point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$, and two nested points of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$ are equal [lem-pc-hilb-nested-points-equal]. Hence $Z(s_{\mathrm{adj}})=Z(\varphi)=D_W$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a $k$-scheme which is proper, smooth of
relative dimension $1$ and geometrically integral over $k$, of genus $g$, with
a $k$-rational point $\sigma$. Let $T$ be a scheme over $k$, write
$f_T:X_T\to T$, and let $D\subset X_T$ be an effective Cartier divisor.

1. $f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_T$-module.
1. (*The $\sigma$-terms cancel.*) If $\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{M}$
for an invertible $\mathcal{O}_T$-module $\mathcal{M}$ and $f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)$ is
invertible, then $f_{T,*}\mathcal{L}$ is invertible and
$$
\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*(f_{T,*}\mathcal{L})^{-1}\;\cong\;
\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\bigl(f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\bigr)^{-1}.
$$
1. (*The adjoint section has zero scheme $D$.*) Let
$\mathcal{L}\in F(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(T)$ ([def-pc-f-subfunctor]),
assume $D\in\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(T)$ ([def-pc-hilb-functor]) and
$\mathcal{L}\cong\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}'$ for some invertible
$\mathcal{O}_T$-module $\mathcal{N}'$, and let $\mathcal{N}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_T$-module with $\mathcal{N}\cong f_{T,*}\mathcal{L}$. Then the section $s$ of
$\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{N}^{-1}$ adjoint to the adjunction map
$f_T^*\mathcal{N}\to\mathcal{L}$ ([lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd]) has zero scheme
$Z(s)=D$.

In particular, for $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$ with universal divisor
$D_{\mathrm{univ}}\subset H\times X$ ([lem-pc-universal-divisor]), the normalized
universal module
$\mathcal{L}_H=\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\otimes\mathrm{pr}_H^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}$
and the open $W\subseteq H$ over which $\mathcal{L}_H$ lies in $F$, the adjoint
section of $\mathcal{L}_H|_{W\times X}$ has zero scheme $D_{\mathrm{univ}}\cap(W\times X)$.

proof.text:
(1) $\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)$ is invertible, hence quasi-coherent, and $f_T$ is
proper (a base change of the proper $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$), hence
quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the direct image of a quasi-coherent module
along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism is quasi-coherent.

(2) By the projection formula ([lem-pc-projection-formula], $q=0$),
$f_{T,*}\mathcal{L}\cong f_{T,*}\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{M}\bigr)\cong
f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes\mathcal{M}$, which is invertible. Hence

$$
\mathcal{L}\otimes f_T^*(f_{T,*}\mathcal{L})^{-1}
\cong\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{M}\otimes
f_T^*\bigl(f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\bigr)^{-1}\otimes f_T^*\mathcal{M}^{-1}
\cong\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\otimes f_T^*\bigl(f_{T,*}\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)\bigr)^{-1}.
$$

(3) Let $\varphi:f_T^*f_{T,*}\mathcal{L}\to\mathcal{L}$ be the adjunction map. The
adjunction map $f_T^*\mathcal{N}\to\mathcal{L}$ is $\varphi$ precomposed with the
isomorphism $f_T^*\mathcal{N}\cong f_T^*f_{T,*}\mathcal{L}$, so it has the same zero
scheme as $\varphi$, and by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd] this is also $Z(s)$; it is a
relative effective Cartier divisor, finite locally free of degree $g$ over $T$.
On the other hand, the canonical section $1$ of $\mathcal{O}_{X_T}(D)$ (the
inclusion $\mathcal{I}_D\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{X_T}$, dualized), twisted by
$f_T^*\mathcal{N}'$, is a morphism $s':f_T^*\mathcal{N}'\to\mathcal{L}$ with zero scheme
$D$ ([def-pc-zero-scheme]). By adjunction $s'$ factors as $f_T^*t$ followed by
$\varphi$, where $t:\mathcal{N}'\to f_{T,*}\mathcal{L}$ is its adjoint; hence
$Z(\varphi)\subseteq Z(s')=D$. Both $Z(\varphi)$ and $D$ are closed subschemes of
$X_T$ finite locally free of degree $g$ over $T$, and a closed immersion between
finite locally free $T$-schemes of the same degree is an isomorphism (on
each fibre it is a surjection of $\kappa(t)$-algebras of the same dimension,
so its ideal vanishes by Nakayama). Hence $Z(s)=Z(\varphi)=D$.

The final assertion is (3) for $T=W$, $D=D_{\mathrm{univ}}\cap(W\times X)$ (a point
of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$, being the restriction of the universal one) and
$\mathcal{N}'=\sigma_W^*\mathcal{O}(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}$.
